query: Help me understand what's in these food-product reviews and what's worth attention or actionable.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a strong grouping axis for understanding the product mix. Categorizations in samples are well-grounded (dog food->pet_food_treat, peanuts/taffy->snack, gelatin confection->snack). The extract sample mapped to condiment_sauce is a defensible but imperfect read; overall soundly derived from text.

per_column.name: taste_quality_verdict
per_column.rationale: A graded taste verdict adds more leverage than a raw Score, giving a comparable quality axis. Sample readings match text ('good quality'->good, 'heaven/flavorful'->excellent, mislabeled peanuts->poor, 'very medicinal'->poor).

per_column.name: texture_quality
per_column.rationale: Texture is a genuine axis when stated, but mostly not_applicable/null. Grounding is weak in samples: dog food labeled 'acceptable' texture with no textural evidence, and taffy labeled 'poor_chewy_tough' despite a positive review—an unwarranted negative inference contradicting the source.

per_column.name: health_dietary_claim
per_column.rationale: Captures organic/gluten-free/etc. claims worth flagging for analysis. Overwhelmingly none_mentioned, and all samples correctly returned none_mentioned where silent—correct behavior.

per_column.name: product_safety_concern
per_column.rationale: Flags actionable safety issues; rare-but-important true class gives leverage. Samples all False, consistent with texts. Being boolean it is somewhat generic but targets a specific actionable signal.

per_column.name: use_case_context
per_column.rationale: Adds a distinct usage/segmentation axis (pet_care, baking, gifting, infant). Samples are reasonable (dog food->pet_care, others->everyday_personal), though everyday_personal is a broad default.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Directly actionable loyalty signal not present in originals. Sample readings sound: mislabeled-peanuts->will_not_repurchase, silent rows->not_stated (correct restraint).

per_column.name: product_consistency_change
per_column.rationale: Detecting formulation/quality drift is actionable, though very rare (2%) and boolean. Sample values (all False) are consistent with texts.

per_column.name: availability_sourcing_note
per_column.rationale: Flags price/delivery/availability mentions, useful for operational attention. Boolean and moderately generic; taffy sample mentions price/delivery yet marked False, a mild miss, but generally grounded.

per_column.name: product_effectiveness_outcome
per_column.rationale: Effectiveness is a meaningful axis for supplements/pet/functional foods, but for generic snacks it largely tracks taste verdict, making it partly redundant. Sample mappings are reasonable (fully/not_effective aligns with sentiment).

judge.rationale: The added columns give multiple genuine, distinct axes—category, graded taste, dietary claims, use case, repurchase intent, and rare-but-actionable safety/consistency flags—that directly serve the query of understanding and triaging reviews. Most values are soundly grounded in the source text, with silent rows correctly defaulted to not_stated/none_mentioned. The main weakness is texture_quality, which shows unwarranted inferences (e.g., positive taffy review tagged poor_chewy_tough), and product_effectiveness_outcome partly restating taste sentiment for non-functional products. Overall a strong, well-grounded set.
